sections.html:
The usual choice is an agent. Some owners sell without one, and some sell outright to a buyer who takes the house in any condition. The deciding factors are the work the house needs and how long you can keep paying its bills.

Huntington sits at the high end of Long Island pricing, and nearly nine in ten of its homes are occupied by their owners. A tidy house in a district buyers ask for can attract plenty of bidders on a regular listing. A house with old systems, a probate holdup or a tenant in place may be better served by a direct sale that closes without fix-up work.

  • Through an agent: wide exposure and often the top price, set against repair costs, showings and a lender's timetable.
  • On your own: the listing fee stays in your pocket, while the contract and marketing work lands on you and your lawyer.
  • Direct as-is: a simpler and faster close with fewer conditions, priced to reflect the buyer's repair bill.

Collect each offer on paper with its closing date, proof of funds and a split of closing costs, then work out what you would really keep.

sections.h2: Where Huntington is and what shapes its housing
sections.html:
Huntington runs along Long Island's North Shore in the northwest of Suffolk County, bordered by the Sound on the north and Nassau County on the west. Four incorporated villages sit within the town: Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport. Everywhere else is a hamlet, including Huntington Station, Dix Hills, Commack, Melville, Greenlawn, Centerport, Cold Spring Harbor, East Northport, Elwood, South Huntington and West Hills. Buyers often search by hamlet or by school district rather than by the town name, so describe your house that way.

Several districts serve the town, including Cold Spring Harbor, Commack, Elwood, Half Hollow Hills, Harborfields, Huntington, Northport-East Northport and South Huntington. Roads include the Long Island Expressway, the Northern State Parkway, Jericho Turnpike (NY 25) and NY 108. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch has stations from Cold Spring Harbor through Northport. A short walk to a station is worth a line in your listing.

Roughly 206,000 people live in the town, a gain of 0.8% since the 2020 base. The 2025 estimate is 205,891 residents in 71,542 households. Owners live in 88.7% of homes. The midpoint value of an owned home is $715,600, the midpoint monthly cost with a mortgage is $3,889, rent at the midpoint is $2,358, and household income at the midpoint is $168,029. The average commute is 35.2 minutes.

Residents 65 and older make up 20.9%, so some sales come from downsizing or an estate. When the seller is an heir, collect the papers showing who may sign the deed before you take offers.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Huntington's Receiver of Taxes collects property tax from December 1 to May 31, in two halves due January 10 and May 31. The office collects for the town, the county and the school districts together, plus other taxing districts. Once January 10 passes, the unpaid first half grows by 1% per month.

Penalty added to the unpaid first half
Pay byPenalty added
February 101%
March 102%
April 103%
May 104%
May 11 to May 315%

Unpaid taxes turn delinquent after May 31, and then the Suffolk County Comptroller is the one to pay. That office adds a 5% penalty and interest of 1% a month counted from February 1, and its phone is 631-852-3000. Tax payments are taken from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays at Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street. Before closing, get the parcel's exact status from the Receiver or your title company so any open balance is cleared at the table.

The complaint, signed, goes to the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. By that rule the next one falls on May 18, 2027, and the Assessor's Office can confirm the date.

An originally signed copy is required, and faxed or emailed complaints are refused. Forms and a fact sheet with instructions are at the Assessor's Office, Room 100 of Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street, Huntington, NY 11743, once April 1 arrives, and they also appear on the Forms and Applications page of the town website.

Because a lower assessment benefits the next owner too, some sellers cite a pending grievance during negotiations. Gather evidence of market value, such as a recent appraisal or sales of similar houses, because the burden of showing that an assessment is too high sits with the owner.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and who records the deed
sections.html:
The state charges $2 for every $500 of price, and unless your contract says the buyer covers it, you pay. Form TP-584 reports it to the county recording officer. Residential prices of $1 million or more add a 1% charge that the buyer bears.

In Huntington the recording officer is the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. Its recording unit receives and examines each instrument and works out the fees, mortgage taxes and transfer taxes owed. Call 631-852-2000 with questions. Your closing lawyer or title company usually carries the deed there. You sign on time and supply a mortgage payoff letter.

sections.h2: Preparing a Huntington house for sale
sections.html: Before offers arrive, confirm three things. First, the exact tax status of the parcel from the Receiver of Taxes or your title company, so no balance surprises you at the table. Second, which of the town's districts and hamlets you will name in the listing, since buyers search that way. Third, whether anyone besides you must sign. For an estate, bring the papers that show who may sign the deed, and for a house with a mortgage, order a payoff letter. A buyer paying cash will still ask for these, and having them ready is what keeps a quick closing quick.

sections.h2: Comparing a direct offer with a listing
sections.html:
Compare what you would keep, not what is advertised. A listing can show a bigger number, but commission, repairs, carrying costs and a financing collapse can all shrink it.

  • Ask the buyer to confirm in writing that nothing is deducted at closing beyond the costs listed in the contract.
  • Find out how long the buyer needs, since a closing date you choose may matter more than a few thousand dollars.
  • Check whether any open tax installments, a mortgage payoff or an estate matter has to be settled before title can pass.
  • Get a second opinion on value from a local agent who knows your hamlet and school district.

faqs.q: What day is Huntington's next Grievance Day?
faqs.a: The town sets it on the third Tuesday of May, so the next is May 18, 2027. Deliver an original signed complaint to the Assessor's Office by then, since faxes and emails are refused.

faqs.q: Where does a Huntington tax payment go once May is over?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Comptroller takes over once May 31 passes. A 5% penalty and monthly interest of 1% from February 1 are added to what is owed.

faqs.q: Does Huntington have any incorporated villages?
faqs.a: Four: Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport. The rest of the town is made up of unincorporated hamlets such as Huntington Station, Dix Hills and Commack.

faqs.q: Who bears the state transfer tax on a Huntington sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, by default. A contract can move it, and the extra 1% on residential prices of $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

faqs.q: Which office files a Huntington deed?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. The office records the deed and collects the fees, mortgage tax and transfer tax due on it, and its phone number is 631-852-2000.
